chapter: Haiti, Artie Shaw and Los Angeles work
title: Victoria Bar and Grill: the tenor saxophone hangout near the Woodside
summary: Hawkins, Dick Wilson, Joe Thomas and Prez gathered at the bar on 141st and Seventh, where players cashed recording checks and spent them.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Oh, it was after that. I think Hawk recorded Body and Soul after the -- you know, he came back -- he came to New York during the war, World War II. That's why he came back, that's what he and Benny Carter first came back from Europe, you know, because of the war, and Hawk recorded this after he came back. [1939] That I'm sure of. But speaking of that during that time when Hawk and Benny Carter came back, we used to go to a club called -- what was the name of this club? The Victoria Bar and Grill. And all the saxophone players, the tenor saxophone players would congregate there every night. There would be Hawk, Dick Wilson. Have you ever heard of Dick Wilson? Dick Wilson was a beautiful tenor saxophone player with Andy Kirk. Joe Thomas with Jimmie Lunceford, Pres. This was just about every night.

Right next door to the Woodside Hotel. It was on 141st I believe and Seventh Avenue. We would go there to cash our recording checks and never get out with a quarter. We would spend the money right in the bar, right there. You know. And Edgar Hayes had the band there. This was a saxophone hangout?
This was a saxophone hangout, and Edgar Hayes. --
Did they ever play pay you there?
This is all they did, they played all

day, just jammed all the time, all night long. And Edgar Hayes had the band there and let's see, the drummer was Kaiser Marshall. You never heard of him but he was a great drummer. But any way this is where we would go to cash our recording checks, and we would just stay right there and spend it. We wouldn't get out with a quarter.
But this was during the time -- this was during the war, you know. Early. Just before we came -- just before we became involved in it. You know the war had started over in Europe.
